title: Bounded Plan, Execute, Verify, Critique, Repair loop
statement: Bounded Plan, Execute, Verify, Critique, Repair loop
body: Accepted. The owner also acknowledged the pinned TypeScript toolchain installed outside the manifest and the loop working values (T25), and allowed constrained agent loop commands (T24). Whether CI should install the toolchain was not decided; CI keeps skipping that scenario. Adopt: - [loop.cjs](../../harness/loop/loop.cjs) with [loop-policy.json](../../harness/policy/loop-policy.json), the CLI [loop.mjs](../../harness/scripts/loop.mjs), and `validate-loop` in `npm run validate` and CI, as described in [LOOP](../loop/LOOP.md). - PASSED reachable only from a verification the loop ran on the final files, plus an independent approval where the task requires one. - Failure classes that stop at once (hard constraint, permission, isolation, sensitive data, missing context, unsafe action, tampering, untracked change), that escalate (repeated failure, budget, non-idempotent failure, blocked review, a policy failure with no declared constraint) or that are repairable within 3 repair attempts and 2 identical failures; a diagnosis with a different approach before any repair that follows a failed repair. - `docs/state/loops/` as a control-plane path. **T24, allowed by the owner:** the `qa-engineer` agent may run exactly `loop.mjs status`, `verify` and `verify-store` on a loop id. Starting, ending, diagnosing, critiquing, cancelling and resuming a loop stay human-run, so an agent can ask the loop to verify but cannot change what it checks, record a review or choose when an attempt ends. `validate-loop` compares the policy grant with the agents' command lists in both directions. - A pinned TypeScript toolchain outside the manifest, verified before use. - No sandbox yet (R15).
subject: adr.0011
